  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><h1 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true"></h1><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">If you are searching for apartments near Washington Square Mall, you are searching in Tigard, Oregon. The mall anchors the north side of this southwest Portland suburb, and the Tigard Triangle, where Highway 217 meets Interstate 5, puts shopping, dining, and an easy commute within a few minutes of home. Montage Tigard sits in that pocket at 13155 SW 68th Parkway, a 183 home community with one and two bedroom apartments plus townhomes, and no studios in its published floor plan lineup.</p><h2 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">What living near Washington Square Mall is actually like</h2><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Washington Square is the center of daily life on this side of Tigard. <a href="https://www.shopwashingtonsquare.com/">Washington Square</a> carries more than 170 stores and restaurants, including the largest Nordstrom in Oregon, Macy's, JCPenney, and Dick's Sporting Goods, so most errands, gifts, and weeknight dinners happen within a short drive.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">You are not limited to one center, either. <a href="https://www.bridgeport-village.com/">Bridgeport Village</a> adds open air shopping and a theater a few minutes south, and <a href="https://www.tigard-or.gov/explore-tigard">downtown Tigard</a> gives you a smaller, walkable local core with independent shops and places to eat. Nike World Headquarters is a short drive north in Beaverton, which matters for a lot of renters who choose this area.</p><h2 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Why renters pick the Tigard Triangle</h2><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">People choose this pocket of Tigard when they want more room and a shorter commute than the city core without giving up convenience. Highway 217 and Interstate 5 meet right here, so Beaverton, Tualatin, Lake Oswego, and downtown Portland are all reachable without crossing the metro. Nearby neighborhoods vary quite a bit in age, price, and feel, which is worth understanding before you sign. Our guide to the <a href="file:///montage-tigard-best-neighborhoods">best neighborhoods in Tigard</a> breaks that down.</p><h2 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">One and two bedroom apartments, no studios</h2><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Floor plan mix is the detail most renters skip when comparing communities near Washington Square, and it is the one that decides whether you actually fit in the home. Some buildings in the area lean heavily on studios and compact one bedrooms.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Montage Tigard publishes one and two bedroom apartments from 686 to 1,338 square feet, plus one, two, and four bedroom townhomes that run as large as 2,281 square feet. There are no studios in the current lineup. You can see the full list on the <a href="https://www.montagetigard.com/floorplans">Montage Tigard floor plans page</a>.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">At 183 homes, it is a smaller community than most of what gets built along the 217 corridor, so it trades the scale of a large complex for a quieter, more personal feel.</p><h2 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">What rent runs near Washington Square in 2026</h2><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">As of July 2026, published one bedroom pricing at Montage Tigard starts around $1,850 a month and two bedrooms start around $2,245, with townhome pricing available by request. Pricing moves with availability and lease term, so treat those as a starting point rather than a quote. For a wider view of what a household actually spends here, including utilities, transportation, and groceries, see our <a href="file:///montage-tigard-cost-of-living">Tigard cost of living breakdown</a>.</p><h2 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Inside the homes and around the community</h2><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Homes feature quartz counters, walnut style cabinetry, stainless steel appliances, plank flooring, 10 foot ceilings, oversized casement windows, and full size in unit washers and dryers. Most homes include a kitchen island, and first floor homes have private patios.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Around the property there is a pool and spa, a sky lounge, a clubhouse, a fitness center, coworking space, a game room with a golf simulator and arcade games, an on site mini market, private garage parking, EV charging, and controlled access entry. The community is pet friendly with a dog park and a pet spa, no weight limit, and breed restrictions that apply. The full list lives on the <a href="https://www.montagetigard.com/amenities">amenities page</a>.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">If you are still deciding whether this side of the metro fits your weekends, our roundup of <a href="file:///montage-tigard-things-to-do">things to do in and around Tigard</a> covers the parks, trails, and local spots people actually use.</p><h2 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">About Montage Tigard</h2><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Montage Tigard is a 183 home community at 13155 SW 68th Parkway, Tigard, OR 97223, near Washington Square Mall and minutes from Highway 217, Interstate 5, and Nike World Headquarters in Beaverton. It offers one and two bedroom apartments plus one, two, and four bedroom townhomes, with no studios in the published floor plan lineup. Community features include a pool and spa, a sky lounge, a clubhouse, a fitness center, coworking space, a game room, an on site mini market, garage parking, and EV charging, and homes include quartz counters and full size washers and dryers. Rates change with availability and lease term.</p><h3 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Are apartments near Washington Square Mall pet friendly?</h3><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Yes. Pet rent and a refundable pet deposit are charged per pet.</p><h3 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">What is there to do near Washington Square Mall besides shopping?</h3><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Beyond Washington Square, renters near the Tigard Triangle in Tigard, Oregon reach Bridgeport Village for open air shopping and a theater, downtown Tigard for independent shops and restaurants, and the Fanno Creek Trail and nearby parks for walking and biking.</p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><h1 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Is Phoenix Back? I'm Not Sure That's the Right Question Yet.</h1><h1 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true"></h1><h1 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true"></h1><h1 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true"></h1><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true"></p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true"></p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true"></p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">There has been a lot of conversation lately about whether the Phoenix apartment market has finally turned the corner.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">It is easy to understand why.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Tours seem steadier. Traffic feels more encouraging than it did before. After a couple of challenging years, demand appears to be showing up again. Across the Phoenix market, more than 4,000 apartment homes were absorbed during the second quarter, well ahead of last year's pace.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">That is encouraging. I'm just not sure I would call it a full recovery yet.</p><h2 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Demand Is Returning, but Rents Have Not Followed</h2><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">What we may be seeing is the beginning of two separate recoveries.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">People are leasing again. More apartment homes are being absorbed, vacancy has improved to approximately 11%, and some of the pressure created by recent oversupply appears to be easing.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">At the same time, average asking rents remain a little more than 2% below where they were last year.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Demand is improving, but pricing power has not fully returned. Those two things can be true at the same time, and they may not recover at the same pace.</p><h2 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Occupancy Still Feels Like Meaningful Progress</h2><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">When rents remain flat or lower, it can be difficult to feel like the market is making progress.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">I tend to look at it a little differently.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">When a community begins leasing more consistently, even at a careful rate, it is rebuilding its occupancy and strengthening its foundation. That may not be the entire recovery, but it is an important part of it.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Occupancy may need to improve before confidence returns, and pricing may simply be the last piece to follow.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">That is why I find the current market encouraging, even if it is not fully where we would like it to be.</p><h2 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">The Supply Picture Is Changing Too</h2><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">The slowing construction pipeline may be one of the more important parts of this story.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Phoenix has worked through a significant wave of new apartment deliveries. Now that pipeline is beginning to thin, with fewer new communities expected to enter the market.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">If renter demand remains steady, reduced supply pressure could eventually create more room for rents to recover. There are still plenty of variables involved, so I see that as a possibility, not a promise.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Still, it is one of the more encouraging changes we have seen in some time.</p><h2 style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">What I'm Watching Next</h2><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">For now, I'm paying attention to the space between improving leasing activity and softer rents.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Are communities holding onto the residents they already have? Are concessions becoming more targeted? Is stronger traffic turning into sustained occupancy? And will demand remain steady as fewer new apartment homes enter the market?</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Those answers will probably tell us more than any single month of leasing activity.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">So, is Phoenix back?</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">I'm not sure that is the right question yet. Phoenix may simply be healing, and that is still worth paying attention to.</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">I would love to hear what others are noticing. Is traffic improving faster than rents in your communities, and does this feel like the beginning of a real shift to you?</p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Melanie Prock<br>President | <a href="https://www.pillarcommunities.com/">Pillar Communities</a></p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p style="text-align:center;white-space:pre-wrap;" class=""><strong>Why Cuvée Apartments is Glendale’s Best Kept Secret Near Westgate</strong></p><p style="text-align:center;white-space:pre-wrap;" class="">If you’ve been searching for an upscale apartment near shopping, nightlife, and stadium energy — welcome to <strong>Cuvée Apartments</strong> in Glendale, AZ. Tucked just minutes from State Farm Stadium and the Westgate Entertainment District, Cuvée is a quiet luxury retreat in the middle of the action.</p><p style="text-align:center;white-space:pre-wrap;" class="">Whether you're a sports fan, foodie, pet parent, or working professional, here's why Cuvée might be Glendale’s best-kept secret.</p><h3 style="text-align:center;white-space:pre-wrap;">✅ 1. It’s the ultimate convenience for Cardinals fans, concert-goers, and anyone who loves being close to the action.</p><h3 style="text-align:center;white-space:pre-wrap;">✅ 2. Designer Apartments with Smart Tech</h3><p style="text-align:center;white-space:pre-wrap;" class="">From sleek quartz countertops to smart home integration, every apartment at Cuvée was built with intention. You'll enjoy stainless steel appliances, wood-style flooring, in-unit laundry, and upgraded finishes throughout — no compromises.</p><h3 style="text-align:center;white-space:pre-wrap;">✅ 3. With outdoor grilling spaces, a dog park, and private coworking areas, Cuvée delivers boutique-style amenities without the high-rise price tag.</p><p style="text-align:center;white-space:pre-wrap;" class="">Ready to see what makes Cuvée so special?<br>Book your private tour today and explore Glendale’s luxury hidden gem → Schedule a Tour</p></div>
